newsitem.title: UK: Cargill says confident of fair IPE probe.
newsitem.headline: Cargill says confident of fair IPE probe.

text.p: Trading house Cargill said on Monday it was confident an International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) inquiry into the November gas oil delivery would be resolved promptly and justly.

"We are confident that when the IPE has had an opportunity to review all the facts that this matter will be resolved promptly and justly," said a statement from Cargill headquarters in Minneapolis in the United States.
Monte Carlo-based AIC, the main short on the contract, declined to comment on an announcement by the IPE that it was launching an investigation into the contract.
The contract was the subject of a tussle between AIC and Cargill that led to a slowdown in Europe's main winter energy market in late November.
Both companies have each suggested the other infringed IPE regulations in carrying out the physical exchange of the material on the Rotterdam region barge market.
The Cargill statement added that Cargill, the dominant long on the contract, had been cooperating fully with the investigation.
"We have made available to the IPE a comprehensive description of our plans to lift the product, including fixtures of barges, inland outlets and storage contracts," the company's statement said.
"We understand the IPE also is investigating the availability of the product at the beginning of the contract delivery period."
